Definition / Description: A relative measure of the effectiveness of training courses.
Answers: Assess perceived effectiveness of training programs to inform L&D investment decisions.
Commentary / Interpretation: Training Quality presents a gauge of the effectiveness of training. While individual organizations may use various survey instruments to assess Training Quality, a commonly used approach is that developed by Donald Kirkpatrick in the late 1950s. Under the Kirkpatrick approach, Training Quality may be assessed at any of four progressive levels. Survey instruments, assessments, tests, and other tools may be used to develop an index for Training Quality at any or all of these levels for various training courses. Level One: Reaction—Measures trainees’ satisfaction with aspects of the training program, including topic, speaker, schedule, etc. Level Two: Learning—Measures the knowledge trainees acquire during the program, including skills improved, attitudes changed, etc. Level Three: Behavior—Measures the extent to which participants change their behavior on the job as a result of knowledge they acquire during training. Level Four: Results—Measures the results of training programs, including higher productivity, improved quality, increased sales, larger profits, reduced turnover, and reduced costs.
Logic: Normalize Likert scale to 0–100 |  Composite index 	 Optional alignment with Kirkpatrick level classification
Notes: Can be segmented by program or delivery channel.

An Employee Commitment Index measures an employee’s attachment and commitment to the firm or corporation. It is based on a number of survey questions that measure employees’ commitment, such as their desire to spend their career with the firm and their views on the firm as a great place to work. Commitment is distinct from employee engagement, which measures the effort and enthusiasm employees put into their daily work. employee commitment for purposes of predicting employee turnover and/or as a tool for analytically deriving the reasons for low commitment so they can be addressed before they lead to turnover issues.

Definition / Description: Relative measure of employees' perceptions of labor market opportunities outside the organization.

Low results for Market Opportunity Index are likely to negatively impact employees’ commitment and likelihood to stay with the organization. Definition / Description: Cost of turnover for employees with less than one year of tenure as a percentage of the total turnover cost.
Formula: Total Termination Value.< 1-Year Tenure / Total Termination Value
Answers: Staffing Effectiveness | Cost of low tenure employee attrition. Also as a measure of staffing effectiveness.
Commentary / Interpretation: Turnover Cost Rate—< 1-Year Tenure measures the percentage of termination costs that come from employees with less than one year of tenure. While this measure does not indicate whether turnover costs among low-tenure employees is high or low, it does indicate the extent to which the turnover costs are driven by low-tenure employees. A result of 40% means that 40% of all termination costs are from these low-tenure employees. Most organizations experience their highest turnover among low-tenure employees. Low-tenure terminations carry with them similar costs and productivity losses to other terminations. However, low-tenure terminations might also signal potential failures of recruiting and onboarding processes. Therefore, New Hire Turnover Contribution can help an employer to approximate the magnitude of turnover costs driven by recruiting and onboarding issues as compared to other potential turnover issues. The higher the result for this measure, the greater the volume of turnover costs that might be prevented through recruiting and onboarding improvement.
Logic: COUNT distinct candidate_id; exclude withdrawn/duplicate; stage-based aggregation where applicable

Logic: COUNT distinct candidate_id; exclude withdrawn/duplicate; stage-based aggregation where applicable
Notes: Use UTC or local consistently.

Definition / Description: Measures how consistently similar candidate profiles receive the same screening decision across reviewers. Why it matters: High variation indicates unstable application of judgment.
Formula: Count of candidates whose final screening decision matches the majority decision within their requisition and score band / Total number of candidates evaluated within the same requisition and screening score band.
Numerator: Count of candidates whose final screening decision matches the majority decision within their requisition and score band.
Denominator: Total number of candidates evaluated within the same requisition and screening score band.
Commentary / Interpretation: High variation indicates unstable application of judgment. Lower rates indicate inconsistent application of rubric-driven decisions and potential human override drift. Persistent instability signals need for calibration review or rubric refinement.
Logic: COUNT distinct candidate_id; exclude withdrawn/duplicate; stage-based aggregation where applicable

Definition / Description: Measures how often screening decisions align with defined must-have criteria and scoring thresholds. Example: Candidate scores 82; threshold is 75; decision = Reject → misalignment. Why it matters: Ensures screening decisions reflect agreed standards.
Formula: Decisions Aligned with Rubric Thresholds / Total Screening Decisions
Logic: COUNT distinct candidate_id; exclude withdrawn/duplicate; stage-based aggregation where applicable

Definition / Description: Measures whether screening score bands meaningfully differentiate downstream candidate performance. Example: Strong band → 70% pass HM screen, Borderline → 35%, Weak → 10% = strong (equal rates across bands = weak signals | Why it matters: Indicates whether screening produces real signal or noise.
Logic: COUNT distinct candidate_id; exclude withdrawn/duplicate; stage-based aggregation where applicable

Definition / Description: Estimates the likelihood that candidates meeting rubric criteria were rejected during screening. Why it matters: Identifies hidden talent loss.
Formula: Qualified Candidates Rejected at Screening / Total Qualified Candidates
Logic: COUNT distinct candidate_id; exclude withdrawn/duplicate; stage-based aggregation where applicable

Definition / Description: Measures whether screening thresholds shift across time or reviewers. Example: Q1 threshold = 70, Q3 threshold = 80 → drift | Why it matters: Prevents silent tightening or loosening of standards. Indicates demand exceeds resources.
Logic: COUNT distinct candidate_id; exclude withdrawn/duplicate; stage-based aggregation where applicable

Definition / Description: Percentage of AI-generated recommendations that were manually overridden by a human decision-maker.
Formula: (AI Recommendations Overridden / Total AI Recommendations Issued) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: High override frequency may indicate: Poor model calibration, Low human trust in AI outputs, Misaligned thresholds, Excessive human discretion | Track trend over time. Segment by recruiter / HM / function.

Definition / Description: Predicted probability that a candidate or employee is open to internal or external mobility based on tenure, career velocity, compensation drift, and engagement patterns.
Commentary / Interpretation: Used for: Proactive retention, Internal talent mapping, External candidate targeting

Definition / Description: Rate of career progression relative to expected progression benchmarks for role, function, and tenure band.
Formula: Actual Career Progression Rate / Expected Benchmark Rate
Commentary / Interpretation: Values >1 indicate accelerated progression Values <1 indicate stagnation risk

Definition / Description: Measures how closely a candidate’s skills align to adjacent or target role skill clusters.
Formula: Cosine similarity between skill vectors (0–100 normalized)
Numerator: Cosine similarity between skill vectors (0–100 normalized)
Denominator: Cosine similarity between skill vectors (0–100 normalized)

Definition / Description: Share of candidate communications responded to within defined SLA window.
Relative availability of qualified talent in market compared to role demand.
Formula: Qualified Talent Pool Size / Open Reqs in Market

Definition / Description: Similar to 4.57 but internal + external combined.
Formula: (Total Qualified Internal Candidates + Qualified External Candidates) / Open Roles
Numerator: Total Qualified Internal Candidates + Qualified External Candidates

Definition / Description: Number of companies hiring for similar role within geographic + function cluster.
Formula: count(Active Job Postings for Similar Roles in Region)
Numerator: Active Job Postings for Similar Roles

Definition / Description: Rate at which compensation expectations exceed internal pay bands.
Formula: Median Candidate Comp Expectation / Internal Median Pay Band

Definition / Description: Share of employees meeting skill + tenure thresholds for internal movement.
Formula: Employees Meeting Mobility Criteria / Total Employees
Logic: Mobility criteria may include: Skill Match + Minimum Tenure + Performance Threshold

Definition / Description: Gap between current workforce skill inventory and future role requirements.
Formula: Required Skills for Strategic Roles − Current Workforce Skill Coverage
Numerator: Required Skills for Strategic Roles − Current Workforce Skill Coverage
Denominator: Required Skills for Strategic Roles − Current Workforce Skill Coverage

Definition / Description: Predictive model estimating capability sufficiency vs strategic demand.
Formula: Projected Workforce Capability Supply / Projected Strategic Capability Demand
Numerator: Current Skill Inventory + Expected Skill Growth + Planned Hiring − Expected Attrition

Definition / Description: Composite of: Time to fill, Offer acceptance, Market density, Compensation drift | Normalized 0–100 difficulty score.
Formula: normalize(Time-to-Fill) + normalize(1 − Offer Acceptance Rate) + normalize(Market Competition Density) + normalize(Compensation Drift Rate) | Composite Score scaled to 0–100
Numerator: normalize(Time-to-Fill) + normalize(1 − Offer Acceptance Rate) + normalize(Market Competition Density) + normalize(Compensation Drift Rate) | Composite Score scaled to 0–100
Denominator: normalize(Time-to-Fill) + normalize(1 − Offer Acceptance Rate) + normalize(Market Competition Density) + normalize(Compensation Drift Rate) | Composite Score scaled to 0–100

Definition / Description: %Evaluations where AI-generated insights informed the final hiring decision

Metric: Staffing Rate - High Potential (% of Workforce)
Definition / Description: Percentage of the workforce designated as high potential.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.High Potential / End of Period Headcount) * 100
Logic: COUNT completions; AVG hours per employee

Metric: LDP - Leadership Dev Plan Prevalence Rate
Definition / Description: Percentage of managers with Leadership Development Plans in place.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Manager.LDP / End of Period Headcount.Manager) *100
Commentary / Interpretation: LDPs might contain planned or recommended steps for a leader related to executive coaching, training courses, supervisory experience, experience in new functions or business lines, mentoring, and other key developmental areas. The plan is targeted toward the leadership competencies or personal skills that have been identified as in need of improvement or generally beneficial to all leaders.
Logic: COUNT completions; AVG hours per employee

Definition / Description: Internal movements of managers between functions as a percentage of total internal movements of managers.
Logic: COUNT internal job changes; filter promotion flag

Definition / Description: Percentage of managerial positions that do not have “ready” candidates identified for potential succession.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Manager.Succession-Applicable.No Ready Candidate / End of Period Headcount.Manager.Succession-Applicable) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: Positions Without Ready Candidates Rate indicates the percentage of managerial positions that require succession management focus but do not have a “ready” candidate identified. A result of 20% means that 20% of succession-applicable managerial positions do not have successor candidates identified that are ready to assume the position immediately if needed.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: The percentage of employees who have had more than one manager within the most recent 12 months.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.>1 Supervisor in Previous 1-Year Period / End of Period Headcount) * 100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount.>1 Supervisor in Previous 1-Year Period
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 30% means that 30% of employees have had a change in direct supervisor within the past year.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Voluntary terminations during the reporting period as a percentage of average headcount.
Commentary / Interpretation: Voluntary Termination Rate measures the percentage of employees who left the organization on their own initiation during the reporting period, for reasons such as resignation or retirement. Voluntary terminations are thus different from involuntary, or employer-initiated, terminations such as firings or layoffs. A result of 15% means that voluntary terminations equated to 15% of the workforce.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees at the end of the period that have less than one year of tenure
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.< 1-Year Tenure / End of Period Headcount) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 10% means that 10% the employee population has less than 1 year of tenure. High levels of less than 1 year of tenure could be a result of rapid growth. More likely, high levels of less than 1 year of tenure is a result of staffing to replace high turnover.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Distribution of headcount by organizational tenure at the end of the reporting period.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.[Tenure] / End of Period Headcount) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: Organization Tenure Staffing Breakdown indicates the percentages of the workforce that fall within various tenure groupings. Graphically, the data are presented as a percentage of the total workforce, i.e., a stacked bar graph.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: The average tenure of the workforce at the end of the reporting period.
Formula: Total Workforce Tenure / End of Period Headcount
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 5.2 means that the average employee has an organizational tenure of 5.2 years.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Temporary employees as a percentage of the total full-time equivalent workforce.
Commentary / Interpretation: Staffing Rate——Temporary indicates the percentage of the organization’’s full-time equivalent workforce that is classified as ““temporary,”” as opposed to ““regular.”” Temporary workers are those who may be employed for a limited duration or those that are otherwise sourced from a temporary employment agency to fulfill short-term staffing needs.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Full-time equivalent employees in revenue-generating roles as a percentage of all full-time equivalent employees.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 20% indicates that one of every five employees serves in a role that creates revenue for the organization.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Part-time employees as a percentage of the total workforce.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Part Time / End of Period Headcount) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 5% means that five of every one hundred employees are classified as part time.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Average number of hours worked per week per employee
Formula: (Hours Worked / Number of Weeks) / Average Headcount
Commentary / Interpretation: Average Workweek measures the number of hours worked per week per employee, on average. A result of 37 means that the average person employed by the organization worked 37 hours per week during the period.
Logic: SUM value; divide by eligible headcount where applicable

Definition / Description: The percentage of employees eligible to receive stock-based incentives.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Stock Incentive Eligible / End of Period Headcount) *100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount.Stock Incentive Eligible
Commentary / Interpretation: A value of 30 indicates that 30% of employees are eligible to receive stock-based incentives.
Logic: SUM value; divide by eligible headcount where applicable

Definition / Description: The average number of stock options granted per eligible employee during the period.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 30 means that employees eligible to receive stock options received 30 options, on average, during the period.
Logic: SUM value; divide by eligible headcount where applicable

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees receiving base salary increases during the reporting period.
Formula: End of Period Headcount.Base Salary Increase / End of Period Headcount * 100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount.Base Salary Increase
Logic: SUM value; divide by eligible headcount where applicable

Definition / Description: Average benefits expense (organization’s contribution) per full-time equivalent employee.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Average total compensation expense, including direct, benefits, and equity compensation, per full-time equivalent employee.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Average direct compensation expense, including wages, bonus, and other cash compensation, per full-time equivalent employee.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Distribution of direct compensation by type, including base, overtime, bonus, incentives, etc.
Formula: (Direct Compensation Expense.[Compensation Type] / Direct Compensation Expense) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: Direct Compensation Breakdown provides the percentages of direct compensation paid that are of various compensation types. Graphically, the data are presented as a percentage of the total direct compensation, i.e., a stacked bar graph. Direct compensation, contrasted with benefits and equity compensation, relates to cash payments for base pay, variable pay, overtime, and other cash payments such as sign-on bonuses and relocation allowances.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees eligible to receive a bonus.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Bonus Eligible / End of Period Headcount) * 100
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status

Definition / Description: Average actual bonus compensation received as a percentage of total potential bonus compensation.
Logic: COUNT active employees; filter employment status
